messages:
incbot: ALERT: Sev2 - OOM spike on node gpu-12 (us-east-1b). Repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts detected by runtime watcher. Affected service: inference-runtime. Ticket INC-12345 created.

carmen_oncall: taking this. seeing steady resident mem climb on nodes serving redwood-13b-qa + paged-attention allocator logs show increasing fragmentation. attaching snippets.

ben_runtime: same cluster. logs show repeated `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` from attention_paged_allocator during long chat sessions. KV cache growth looks non-evicting; free list fragmented into many small slabs.

alice_sre: any customer impact yet?

carmen_oncall: yes — brief 5xx spike ~04:12-04:18 UTC for Searchly (prod-us-east). auto-fallback to smaller variant triggered for some calls, but a subset hit the overloaded nodes and got 503s.

dave_prod: confirmed. Searchly reported degraded latency and some failures. They were routed to fallback but stateful conv sessions got 503s on reconnect. Already opened support ticket.

ben_runtime: quick triage: paged allocator appears to slowly leak effective usable memory because many tiny free fragments are left behind when KV entries churn. combined with long-lived prefix cache for a few heavy customers, fragmentation creeps until container OOMs.

carmen_oncall: mitigation plan I started: 1) cordon+drain gpu-12 to remove flapping instance from lb. 2) trigger `kv-compact` job on that AZ to attempt coalescing free lists. 3) temporarily increase evict aggressiveness for KV cache for heavy customers (`KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6 -> 0.4`) 4) rollback last model rollout to non-paged variant for redwood-13b-qa if compaction doesn't help.

ben_runtime: commands I ran (FYI):
```
# drain node
kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# run compaction (dry-run first)
./ops/kv-compact --az us-east-1b --target=attention_paged --dry-run
# enable aggressive reclaim for runtime
kubectl set env deploy/inference-runtime KV_EVICT_AGGRESSIVE=true -n prod
```

alice_sre: good. Any risk of compaction causing transient latency?

ben_runtime: compaction will pin pages briefly; we expect small latencies on compaction workers. Doing node-by-node reduces customer impact. We should avoid global compaction during peak.

elaine_pm: timeline and customer comms?

carmen_oncall: immediate comms: sent Searchly ops a note that we're investigating and have isolated a flapping node; asking to defer heavy batch jobs for 1 hour. Postmortem and RCA will follow. I'm going to watch the compaction run and the mem profiles for 2 hours.

dave_prod: Searchly asked if this is a regression — they saw steady increase in errors after yesterday's canary. Could be related to usage patterns.

ben_runtime: note — allocator change in nightly (ATTN_PAGED_ALLOW_SPARSE_FREE=1) may have increased free-list fragmentation for workloads with lots of small KV churn. I'm rolling that flag back on canary hosts.

carmen_oncall: action items captured: [1] finish compaction job on us-east-1b (in progress) [2] rollback sparse-free flag on canary (ben) [3] keep gpu-12 drained and replace before rejoin (infra) [4] lower KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD for heavy customers (ops) [5] prepare fallback routing to quantized-8b variant if errors persist (prod) [6] collect heap/fragmentation snapshots and upload to INC-12345 (carmen/ben).

alice_sre: set pager_notify to eng-oncall if another OOM happens within 30m. Also add alert for fragmentation ratio >0.75.

incbot: BOT: compaction job reported: us-east-1b attention_paged compaction started at 04:24 UTC; estimated run 8m/node; progress: 1/3 nodes complete.

carmen_oncall: compaction finished on first node, memory reclaimed ~18GB usable, no crashes after drain. continuing to monitor.

ben_runtime: rolled back `ATTN_PAGED_ALLOW_SPARSE_FREE` on canary hosts. observing reduced free-list churn metric. will keep this rollback until we have a safer allocator patch.

dave_prod: Searchly ops acknowledged, holding off on heavy jobs. I'll coordinate follow-up comms after 2h stable window.

carmen_oncall: marking handoff: I'll watch for 2 hours, then escalate to eng-oncall if fragmentation resurges. If stable, we'll move to RCA prep and longer-term fixes: allocator coalescing improvements, background compaction daemon, and stronger per-customer eviction isolation.

alice_sre: noted. Adding postmortem owner: ben_runtime. Please include timeline and the canary flag correlation.

incbot: RESOLUTION PLAN: node drained + replaced, compaction reclaimed memory, rollback of sparse-free flag on canary, temporary evict policy tightened. Monitoring window: 120m. If errors recur escalate to Sev1.

carmen_oncall: handing off to ben_runtime for RCA and follow-ups. I'm available if it flares. :thumbsup:

ben_runtime: taking RCA. starting artifact collection now (heap dumps, allocator histograms, KV churn traces). I'll post updates to INC-12345 and ping eng-oncall if we see reoccurrence.

carmen_oncall: thanks — closing thread for now, will reopen if anything changes.
